limitations: Reviewer is a separate AI agent session on the same host and the same operator account as the producer. It is not a second machine, a second operator, or a human. Same-host agent reviewer. It ran no harness, used no network, changed no git state and no repository file. Code and documents were read from a snapshot (commit 573b146; not checked against git). Private scratch files were deleted.

This is a delta review of openclaw-public-candidates-v6 against the approved v4 (review openclaw-independent-public-review-v4) and against v5, which this reviewer rejected for two false statements in the adapter document. Delta review: the semantic checks of earlier reviews carry over only for files that are byte-equal. 210 of 224 files are byte-equal to v5 and to v4; this includes every native file, every input (observer, workload, context, capture documents, both inventories, the capture assertion, the transformation receipt) and every runtime source. The 14 files that differ are, per run: manifest.json, the bound adapter document (runtime/docs/survival-v1/adapters/openclaw.md, equal to the snapshot at 573b146), the replay receipt and the private-transformation sidecar (a parent manifest digest); plus the bundle (3 values: the digest of the adapter document in one locator per run) and summary.json. Sets v1, v2, v3 and v5 must never be published as evidence of this row (v5 holds the false statements). The reviewer re-read the differing files. Previous sets that held a private-derived value must never be published.

Row delta. All 31 rows of the three runs equal the saved replays of v4 and of v5 (88.093, 88.111, 88.093; aggregate 88.099 as in v4). Only the format-evidence locator digest of the adapter document differs.

The previous sets (openclaw-public-candidates-v1, -v2 and -v3) must never be published as evidence of this row. Set v3 holds 60 distinct digests of metadata listings of the owner's home (entries_sha256 and directory_sha256 of the digested subtrees that changed); the reviewer found none of them in v4; the files are byte-equal in v6. Previous sets that held a private-derived value must never be published. The sidecar files beside the packets (summary.json, *-private-transformation.json, *-receipt.json, *-tamper.json) hold digests of private files and must not be published.

Change of this set. Every entries_sha256 and every value of directory_sha256 of a digested subtree (8 subtrees, 2,968 digests per inventory) is 64 zeros in state-before and r2-state-after. In v3, 2,956 of the 2,968 were already zeros; the 12 per inventory that differed between the two inventories held real digests (60 distinct values in the three runs). Where a digest differs between the two inventories (12 values per run, the entries digest of one subtree and 11 directory digests), state-after holds the word changed padded with underscores to 64 characters. The receipt (r2-native-receipt.json) holds the same zeros and the word in before.entries_sha256 and after.entries_sha256 of its shared entry; its inventory digests, metadata digests and the digests that bind the changed files are recomputed. No metric row changes: the reviewer compared all 31 rows of the three runs with the saved replays of v3 (equal); only the digests of the format-evidence locators for the documentation and the three capture documents differ, and the scores are equal (88.093, 88.093, 88.111; aggregate 88.099).

Check of the digest removal. The reviewer collected every entries_sha256 and directory_sha256 value (2,979 distinct non-zero values) from the private parent openclaw-score-replay-v4 and searched all 224 files in plain, upper-case, base64, base64 of the hex text, UTF-16 and 20-character-prefix forms, with Zstandard blobs decompressed: none occurs. 60 of them occurred in set v3. The replay's receipt check (verify_state_receipt) passes on the public inventories and gives the same classes as v3 (the 4 digest fields of the shared entries are the only difference). It passes for the right reason: it compares whether a digest differs. Two controls on the public inventories (the receipt re-bound to the changed inventory): changing every word to zeros, and changing one unchanged zero to the word, are each rejected with 'whole-home classification differs from the receipt'. The word is constant (the string changed plus underscores) and leaks nothing: the fact that those directories changed is already public in changed_directories and in the entry times.

What stays readable about the digested subtrees. The 8 roots keep their real relative path, device number, inode, birth, modification and change time in nanoseconds, entry count and size. The inner directory structure stays as an aliased tree (equal length names), so depth, fan-out and name lengths are readable. The 36 receipt-class directories, the 28 directories above a classified entry and the 11 links of a receipt class keep inode, size and times as well. The 2 Codex session-store files that no receipt class lists keep their three times. The reviewer judges this as machine-state metadata that holds no content, account or identity value, but that is a stable fingerprint of the owner's machine (same inode and birth_ns in all three packets for 31 entries; mtime_ns differs for 13 of them). The owner may want those fields blanked too. The adapter document now states this correctly (see the next limitation); the false statements of v4 and v5 are gone.

Adapter document, section 'Machine values that stay'. The reviewer did not trust the script scripts/tabulate_openclaw_machine_values.py. It recomputed both tables from the public inventories (state-before.json, r2-state-after.json) and receipts of the three packets: every entry was classed by kind and by receipt class (directories_changed, run_owned, session_owned and the paths of shared_changed), the directories above a classified entry, the digested roots and the two session-store files; for each field it counted kept and blanked values, per run, before and after. Every cell and every count of the first table (9 rows; counts such as 120/122/119/121/120/122 and 9409/9409/9414/9414/9415/9415) and of the second table (4 rows; 25/2/25/2/25/2, 2, 120/115/119/114/120/115, 11) equal the bound document; no field is mixed inside a row. The sentences below the tables hold: one device value for all entries and a real root_identity (the same in every inventory); 8 digested roots, 36 and 28 directories and 11 links keep inode, size and the three times; files of a receipt class and the 2 store files keep the three times and have inode and size blanked; the 4 links in no class and every other unclassified entry keep only device; the receipt keeps size_bytes for directories, links and digested roots, blanks it for files, and keeps entry_count only for the 2 digested roots of the class; the three class lists hold paths only; 31 entries have a real inode and birth_ns in all three packets, all equal, and mtime_ns differs for 13. The definition 'blanked = a 1 followed by zeros' matches the sanitizer (_blank keeps the digit count) and no kept cell contains such a value by accident. entry_count is never blanked: the sanitizer does not touch it and its values are 1, 4, 14, 87, 646, 6660, 7796. The kept digit count is honestly stated: the document says a blanked size keeps its order of magnitude (it is the same for inode and times, where the digit count is constant). Not in the section, and not machine values in its sense: started_ns of the receipt, the sizes of the copied artifact files and of the store exports (stated elsewhere in the document).

Environment of the runs: the owner's normal OpenClaw state and login, not an isolated state; OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8) with the codex harness plugin, which runs a Codex app server; the owner's default model (openai / gpt-5.6-terra), not a pin of the benchmark; the owner's configuration, skills and workspace files were in the context. Capture route: a foreground gateway and one ACP process started by the controller, with channels and timed jobs switched off. One model, one build, one day, one machine. Capture authenticity rests on the producer's capture documents; the captures are bound to the controller by schema and plan documents only.

Native record. An OpenClaw session has no file of its own. The scored record is the rows of the session in three tables of the shared agent store (transcript_events, trajectory_runtime_events, session_windows), exported by owner permission from a private temporary copy and bound as a JSON row export with the vendor schema. The rules of the rubric were written before this row, but the read was chosen after the containers were seen and after its point effects were estimated; the rubric table got the OpenClaw row only after the first review. Reviewer judgment: the read is a fair description of the format. Every scored fact comes from the three tables; a wider read (Codex rollout, ACP replay buffer) gives the same points; a read without the trace table loses points; no other read gives more.

Usage judgments accepted with reservation. The usage object on the displayed response is the total of the run (all model requests of the turn); the rubric allows a turn scope (5 and 4 points if a reader requires records per request). Reconciliation is no longer credited (see above). cacheWrite is an explicit 0 on the response; the format also writes 0 as a placeholder on other assistant messages, so that 0 is weak evidence (4 points).

Other scoring judgments accepted. The two forms of one tool call (the model's exec script and the bash or apply_patch execution) are one event stated twice, as the Codex CLI row treats the same pattern: each script holds exactly one tool call with the same command and directory or the same patch; this costs the row its duplicate safety (about 7.3 points lost on actions, results and relations if the script form counted as extra actions). The exit code comes from the trace table joined by toolCallId, inside the read, and isError agrees (3.75 points). The harness name comes from traceSchema openclaw-trajectory; no row has a product field (2 points). Zstandard counts as a commodity parser, as for the DeepSeek Harness row; without it a reader loses the first prompt (2 points). Duplicate safety is printed as native_absent for a zero count; it is a measured zero.

Observer. It is rebuilt in the closed replay from the ACP stream of each turn, the helper ledger and the file hashes; no native row is read. The stream is made by the same gateway process that writes the native rows, as stdout streams are in other rows. It shows only the execution form of a tool call and no output text: helper output lines come from the helper ledger, and a helper that is not the last segment of a compound call takes its exit code from the ledger. The model comes from one start line of the gateway, per process. The stream does not show the commentary messages; the native final message is marked by runTerminal.

Replaced attempts and waiver. Scheduled attempts -03 (repetition 1, controller guard fault at the native bracket) and -05 (repetition 2, turn 1 ended with no visible response on the stream) were replaced by -04 and -07; -07 ran after -06. The rubric rule 'Do not replace a scheduled run with calibration or a corrective attempt' is waived for v1 by the owner on 2026-10-08, after the results were known; the rubric carries a dated waiver note and the adapter document (section 'Replaced attempts', now current in the packets) lists each replaced attempt and its reason. The reviewer cannot verify the owner decision, only that the documents state it. The native state of -05 was never taken, so what its session recorded is unknown. The consequence for ranking is the owner's and must be disclosed in the report.

Public derivative, not raw capture. At equal file byte length: home name and e-mail aliased; tool and schema descriptions of the trace rows blanked; every value of a table outside the read blanked except ids of the test session; slash command lists of the ACP stream blanked; unclassified inventory names aliased and their metadata blanked; all mirror fingerprints zeroed; all digests of digested subtrees zeroed (see above). The compressed first prompt is not the vendor's bytes: the sanitizer wrote a new Zstandard frame from the event text with the fingerprint zeroed and appended a skippable frame of zeros to keep the length. This is unchanged from v3 (the row export is byte-equal); the reviewer re-checked that a plain Zstandard reader reads it and that the 31 rows do not change.

Privacy checks and their limits (v6). The reviewer searched all 224 files and file names for the home name, the operator e-mail and local part, every organisation-, key- and token-like value and every id-like value of the private parent, in plain, lower, upper, reversed, hex, base64 (three alignments, URL-safe), UTF-16, percent and SHA-1/256/512/MD5 forms: no hit except the test-session ids (three per-run key ids and one owner label of the test session, which the packets state on purpose) and common words. Every /Users/ path holds the alias. check_public_packets, called as the sanitizer calls it (the sanitizer's digest and hex allowlists, the three fresh replay receipts, the bundle as extra file), reports 1393 public-bytes digests, 532 replay-output digests, 24 allowlisted digests (store schema digests), no unbound digest and no unlisted hex run (zero 59, decimal 174056, constant 9, uuid 4152, provider id 82, allowlisted 3); short_digest_warnings is empty. The classes equal v4. The 103,789-digest search of the v4 review and the Zstandard decompression scan were not repeated: all data files are byte-equal to v4. A scan cannot prove the absence of a private value in a form that was not tried; the gateway token was never available to the reviewer.

Locator binding (v6). The observer sha256 of each pair equals inputs/observer.json, the native manifest sha256 equals native/decode.json, and 108 file locators (native capture files, the adapter document, the receipt and both inventories) equal public files by sha256. The bundle differs from v5 in exactly 3 values, the digest of the adapter document. The row locators of the density metric and the nine 'outside-the-read' locators (bound by size only; not in the packets; 72 percent of the density denominator) carry over from v4: their files are byte-equal and the fresh replay equals the bundle. The fixed observer label 'openclaw-whole-home-receipt' is a bundle label, not an id in observer.json.
